Inspect saved allocation fits without recomputation

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R, R/06-ae_methods.R, R/06-ae_multistart.R
allocation-fit-methods.Rd

A fit from fit_allocation() keeps every start and the selected fit, fit$best; both have these methods, which read what the fit saved. Coefficients and fitted targets are read from the selected fit. Multistart summaries retain failed starts, boundaries, warnings/errors and descriptive disagreement. A search with no eligible fit remains inspectable by summary, while coefficient and fitted extraction fail clearly. print() of a fit shows its starts and the one selected; print() of the selected fit shows its estimates, loss and convergence, and its summary() adds the ranges of the fitted values, of the model state and of the residuals.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ae_problem_nfxp_fit'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_multistart_fit'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_problem_nfxp_fit'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_multistart_fit'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_multistart_fit'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_problem_nfxp_fit'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_multistart_fit'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ae_problem_nfxp_fit'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.ae_problem_nfxp_fit'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

object, x

A fit from fit_allocation() (an ae_multistart_fit) or its selected fit fit$best (an ae_problem_nfxp_fit); for the print method of a summary, the summary of the selected fit.

...

Additional generic arguments; currently unused.

digits

Significant digits of the printed numbers.

Value

coef() returns the saved named parameter vector. fitted() returns saved canonical fitted targets. summary() of a fit returns a list containing the selected fit summary, per-start table, boundaries, disagreement and messages; summary() of the selected fit returns its model and family, its parameters, its loss and convergence, and the ranges of the fitted values, of the state and (when the fit kept its observed values) of the residuals. print() returns its input invisibly. These diagnostics establish neither identification nor global optimality.

See also

fit_allocation()

Examples

# West Cornwall: the small areas and practices west of easting 170 km
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)
areas <- areas[!areas$scilly & areas$cent_x < 170000, ]
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
gp <- gp[!gp$scilly & gp$easting < 170000, ]
inputs <- prepare_allocation(stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa),
                             stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice),
                             cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice])

# A fit to the registrations of these residents at these practices
flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &
                          cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]
totals <- sapply(split(flows$patients, flows$practice), sum)
fit <- fit_allocation(clm_allocation(inputs, fit_v0 = TRUE), totals,
                      loss = "poisson")

# The selected estimates and the modeled registrations at each practice
coef(fit)
#>     sigma        v0 
#> 13.223212  1.001842 
round(fitted(fit))
#> L82018 L82036 L82038 L82041 L82042 L82044 L82047 L82056 L82059 L82068 L82070 
#>  17829  15924  13051  22441  11935  10758   6762   2851   3674   7954   5444 
#> L82620 Y01050 Y01051 Y01922 
#>   3535  10004   3367  10545 

# Every start, the selected fit and its residuals
summary(fit)
